papers.title_en: TaCo: Rethinking Correlation for Visual Tracking on Edge Devices
papers.authors: Qingmao Wei, Fagui Liu, Quan Tang
papers.evidence: 面向边缘设备的视觉目标跟踪器设计
papers.tldr: 轻量级跟踪器普遍用注意力替代互相关，但在低功耗边缘硬件上，softmax、归一化与重塑等内存受限算子的耗时远超预期。论文在边缘NPU与Arm CPU上以统一验证协议基准测试高效跟踪器，发现互相关跟踪器速度更快但精度落后。作者重新审视互相关在模板-搜索交互中的不足，并提出改进的相关性跟踪方法。实验表明该方法在保持速度优势的同时提升精度，为边缘设备实时视觉跟踪提供了兼顾效率与准确率的方案。
papers.abstract_en: Lightweight trackers have replaced cross-correlation with attention, and on low-power edge hardware they pay for it, since memory-bound softmax, normalization and reshaping operators of attention cost far more time than their arithmetic suggests. Benchmarking efficient trackers on an edge Neural Processing Unit (NPU) and an Arm CPU under one numerically validated protocol, we find that correlation trackers are the fast ones, but they lag in accuracy unless they adopt a ViT backbone, which brings attention back. We revisit what correlation lacks. Template--search interaction serves two roles: conditioning the search features on the target and matching them against it spatially. Attention does both, whereas correlation only matches, and does so on features extracted without knowledge of the target. We present TaCo (Target-aligned Correlation), which supplies the missing conditioning without attention by letting the template enter the per-frame network only as operands computed once per video. A descriptor of the target scales and shifts the search features channel by channel inside the backbone, and kernels aligned with the target box, each with a weight predicted from the template, correlate with them in one matrix product. With the backbone fixed, our correlation remains essential while incurring negligible NPU overhead, offering a better speed-accuracy trade-off than the attention-based interactions we tested. TaCo-T achieves 62.3% LaSOT AUC at 184 FPS on the Rockchip RV1126B NPU and 96 FPS on a Raspberry Pi 5 CPU, 3.0x and 3.5x the NPU speed of HiT-Tiny and AsymTrack-T at higher accuracy. TaCo-B reaches 65.6% at 50 FPS on the NPU, more than twice the speed of HiT-Base, AsymTrack-B and LightFC-vit, again at higher accuracy. Code and models are available at https://github.com/TsingWei/TaCo-Tracker.

papers.title_en: CalibTrack: Exploring Learned Heteroscedastic Covariance for Robust Multi-Camera Pedestrian Tracking
papers.authors: Jack Roberts, Aditya Iyer, Nora Ayanian
papers.evidence: 视频中的多相机行人多目标跟踪
papers.tldr: 多视角多目标跟踪系统依赖测量协方差来引导关联、融合与状态估计，但这些协方差通常是需手工调参的启发式估计。作者研究学习到的异方差测量协方差对多相机跟踪校准与鲁棒性的影响，并提出CalibTrack，用逐检测协方差替代统一协方差。在WildTrack与MultiviewX上结合多种分析型跟踪器进行评测。结果表明该方法提升了跟踪的校准性与稳健性，为多相机跟踪提供了新思路。
papers.abstract_en: Analytical multi-view multi-object tracking (MV-MOT) systems rely on measurement covariance estimates to guide association, fusion, and state estimation. These covariance estimates are typically heuristic, requiring hand-tuning to the specific deployment scenario. We investigate how learned heteroscedastic measurement covariance affects calibration and robustness in analytical multi-camera tracking. To support this analysis, we introduce CalibTrack, a detector-side predictor that replaces uniform measurement covariance with per-detection covariance. We evaluate CalibTrack on the WildTrack and MultiviewX pedestrian tracking datasets with multiple analytical tracker cores, including an identity-informed GM-PHD, JIPDA, and pruned delta-GLMB filter. We additionally evaluate robustness by simulating adverse weather conditions with stable diffusion, Gaussian noise, camera browning, and camera dropout. CalibTrack improves average adverse tracking performance over confidence-scaled covariance, while producing better calibrated predictions, indicating the value of heteroscedastic covariance within analytical tracking. Comparisons with stronger heuristic covariance methods show that the benefits of learned covariance remain bounded by the quality of available observations and the downstream tracker choice. Together, these findings provide a principled exploration of learned covariance estimation and its potential for uncertainty-aware analytical tracking.

papers.title_en: Towards 360$^\circ$ Embodied UAV Tracking Without Turning
papers.authors: Bingyu Li, Wu Du, Zhiyuan Zhao, Junyu Gao, Xuelong Li
papers.evidence: 无人机视觉目标跟踪基准与视觉语言动作跟踪器
papers.tldr: 该文指出现有具身无人机跟踪将目标可见性与航向控制耦合，目标一旦离开前视相机视野便失效。作者提出利用全向球面感知在无需转向的情况下跟随指定目标，构建包含2652条序列、超173万同步观测和八类跟踪任务的360UAV-ETrack仿真基准，并提出融合持续视觉指代、压缩时序记忆与几何对齐轨迹监督的全景视觉语言动作框架。实验在多个跟踪任务与闭环场景上验证其有效性，为空中视觉目标跟踪提供了新设定与评测平台。
papers.abstract_en: Conventional embodied UAV tracking couples target observability with heading control because targets may leave the field of view of forward-facing cameras. We investigate a complementary paradigm that uses full-spherical perception to follow designated targets without active heading adjustment. To support this setting, we introduce 360UAV-ETrack, a simulation benchmark comprising 2,652 sequences, over 1.73 million synchronized observations, eight tracking tasks, and 150 held-out closed-loop scenarios. We propose 360UAV-TVLA, a panoramic vision--language--action (VLA) framework integrating persistent visual referring (PVR), compressed temporal memory (CTM), and geometry-aligned trajectory supervision (GTS) for instance identification, motion reasoning, and three-dimensional control. Experiments across two VLA backbones show consistent gains over standard fine-tuning, with normalized average tracking frames increasing from 22.56\% to 35.28\% for $π_0$ and from 25.68\% to 33.64\% for $π_{0.5}$. Our benchmark further reveals a substantial gap between offline imitation accuracy and closed-loop tracking reliability, establishing a challenging testbed for future research https://libingyu01.github.io/360UAV-ETrack_360UAV-TVLA/

papers.title_en: Tracktail: Multi-View 3D Point Tracking without Depth Input
papers.authors: Katie L Rupp, Jonathan Wong, Sharmishtaa Seshamani, Ana Mafalda Vicente, Lili Karashchuk
papers.evidence: 跨多视角视频跟踪三维查询点
papers.tldr: 现有三维点跟踪方法通常依赖深度输入，限制了多视角场景下的应用。本文提出Tracktail架构，将任务分解为逐相机视频特征编码与逐查询解码器，仅在解码器中对查询执行跨相机注意力，从而实现高效推理。同时引入基于相机几何的逐相机场景尺度，以归一化不同数据集的尺度，并在合成多视角Kubric与新基准上训练。该方法在无需深度输入下实现高效三维点跟踪，为多视角视频理解提供了实用方案。
papers.abstract_en: We introduce Tracktail, a novel architecture designed to efficiently track query points in 3D from multiple calibrated views without any depth input. Our architecture separates the task as a per-camera video encoding of features and a per-query decoder. Notably, camera cross-attention is only performed across queries in the decoder, allowing for efficient inference (7 FPS and less than 4 GB memory for 10 views and 100 query points). We further introduce a per-camera scene scale computed from camera geometry, which allows us to normalize inputs and predictions appropriately across a vast variety of dataset scales. We train on a synthetic Multi-View Kubric dataset as well as a novel Multi-View Point Odyssey benchmark dataset, which consists of synthetic renders of humans and animals across 499 frames. Tracktail achieves state-of-the-art results on the Panoptic Studio, DexYCB, and Multi-View Kubric benchmarks, outperforming methods that rely on estimated depth. Tracktail also demonstrates a strong ability to maintain accurate tracking over longer ranges compared to existing methods. Our code, data, and weights are publicly available: https://ai-hhmi.github.io/tracktail/
